repo: a document folder for an invoicing SaaS where a founder pitched, in two lines, 'make invoice PDFs real-time by moving PDF generation to an edge function'. Files: the pitch note, current architecture notes, a per-request latency CSV for PDF generation (invoice page count, milliseconds, about 3,000 rows, mostly small invoices), a support-ticket export (complaints are about large invoices only), a cost sheet, a vendor free-tier limits note (CPU seconds and memory per call), a team calendar (two engineers, one on leave for two of the five working days before a quarter freeze), an incident postmortem, a README. About 22 files.
idea: An architect turns a vague idea into a bounded spike with a falsifiable result. Seed: the headline average latency (dominated by small invoices) is a decoy; the complaints and the support target (a stated p95 for large invoices) concern invoices over 20 pages, whose p95 a script computes from the CSV; the vendor limits would break above a page count the CSV shows exists; only 8 engineer-days are free, not 10. Output: a spike plan ending with a JSON block: question, hypothesis, metric, baseline {value, sample, source}, pass_threshold, kill_threshold, timebox_days, engineer_days, steps (each with name, days), scope_in, scope_out, decision_rule. A hidden script checks that the baseline is the large-invoice p95 from the data (about 5%), the pass threshold is tied to the support target, the plan fits the free engineer-days, and the kill criterion is numeric and different from the pass one.
